results.title: just ok
results.text:
I thought it would be interesting to watch the cremation ceremony, but I didn't realize it would be uncomfortable (at least for me) seeing corpse plus the smell of the smoke too. I saw some people wearing mask so I suggest you bring one. 

There is nothing much to see on the temple itself because it is for Hindu only.  But overall it was a new experience for me.

Entrance fee for foreigners is 1000. And taxi from here to Thamel costs 300. Not sure though it if is a good deal, but I think yes it is, considering the traffic in Kathmandu.

results.title: Once in a lifetime
results.text: This place has made me rethink my ideas on death itself. I must admit it's quite a shock to see the cremations from up close but it's beautiful in it's own way, very educational as a Westerner.

results.title: lighting ceremony
results.text: While the Pashupati Natu in itself it is beautiful. Much history. Over 1000 people cremated there a day. The ceremony began a 7 pm . It was beautiful to me as a send off of the soul leaving the body and let the familys, while sad, help celebrate that their soul has moved on. May bother some but I loved it.

results.title: Pashupatinah Temple
results.text: There is a river where they put the dead after burning them. And places for women and men to pray, separately (It's a temple). And those funny and cheerful holy men! And the monkeys are not missing, they are always feeding themselves in the place. Nice, picturesque, I only was not interested in cremations.

results.title: Impressive view at the cremation ceremonial atPasupati
results.text: Kailash Travel advised us to go here and they were right, walking up the lane to the temple we found the Nepali buying ceremonial things for the cremation ceremonial. We were really impressed.

results.title: Don't go at dusk!
results.text: I was really looking forward to witnessing this Hindu ritual and although the temple is always open, I later learned that no cremation occurs after dusk.  There were very few people there, the holy men had all gone home and other than the structure itself, there wasn't much to see. I should have done my research to maximize my experience and show the respect this site deserves.

results.title: Beautiful and spiritual
results.text: The temple was beautiful. The arts of dwelling is awesome and the burning carcass make you think of life. The temple is one of the must visit place in Kathmandu. Perfect to visit at evening during aarati

results.title: Moving
results.text: This is a great stop if you have some time to kill before you fly out of Kathmandu as it is right next to the airport.  Go in the late afternoon/early evening if you can.  This was one of the highlights of my trip.  You can really feel the spirituality and history in this place,

results.title: Very spiritual place
results.text: I was in awe of the spiritual vibes and history of this sacred place. I spent several hours here and was really glad I made this visit a part of my trip

results.title: Witnessing cremation rituals
results.text: If you walk here from Boudhanath, you could enter from near the river without any entrance fees. Managed to witness the cremation process which was quite an eye opener.

results.title: Fascinating but maybe choose your time (if not Hindu)
results.text: This is, apparently, a very important location for Hindu people and that was clear today. Nepal New Year was probably not the best day to visit! Very interesting with many holy men on site. Walked through to the deer park and down to the river on the far side. So many monkeys!

results.title: Fascinating!
results.text: We didn’t go inside the temple as we aren’t Hindu but did go out to see where 24 hour cremations take place on the bank of a small river.  An absolutely fascinating place. Loved it here.

results.title: Trip to Nepal
results.text: Pasupathinath temple was a relief to the mind and soul. Although access road was in bad shape, it was pleasant clean and spiritual inside. A long queu did not hamper the feelings. It was indeed a cleansing occasion

results.title: Get your spirituality shaken a bit !
results.text: It is a must if you just want to learn a little more about your spirituality and the values that It can deeply take when you enter in to other ways of tkinking. We don't have to agree or disagree, just take it as another approach to open our  mind on human beings !

results.title: Highlight of our Kathmandu visit
results.text: We had half a day free and someone recommended that we visit this temple to better understand the people of Nepal. When we walked in, I remember thinking that I have no idea what I am looking at as there are no helpful and informative signs in English. You have to pay 1000 Nepali rupee entrance fee so understanding what is going on would be nice! A helpful young man introduced himself and asked if we wanted a tour. Price for a guide seems to be 1000 for about an hour but we bargained for 900 as we could more easily split the sum by the 3 of us. This guide was  called Sumit Kharel Highly recommend him! It’s a fascinating place but you do need a guide to explain everything. Much of it was damaged in the 2015 earthquake but the biggest and holiest temple was unscathed. Only Hindu’s can enter though. Probably the most fascinating part was seeing how they burn the bodies next to the holy( but grubby ) river called Bagmati River. It feeds into the Ganges. The kids try to fish out coins with a magnet but honestly... you would not want to be near that water! There is an old people’s home in the compound and a hospice next to the cremation area. Our tour lasted about 90 minutes and we paid up the requested  1000 rupees... it was worth every one of them!

results.title: Place of Worship
results.text: Visited on a Festival day.  Was wonderful to see so many happy families in their colourful Saris celebrating their faith.  Further exploration of the site took us to the cremation area.  As an Australian it was confronting to witness a cremation in progress and I felt for the grieving families but It was an interesting experience.  A definite must do.

results.title: Interesting to learn about Nepalese traditions and beliefs.
results.text: Visited this temple as part of a full day sightseeing tour with Himalayan Social Journey. Very interesting commentary from our guide and whilst most westerners might find it a little bit morbid to visit such a public cremation site, it was still good to see and learn about the Nepalese traditions and beliefs. Quite emotional but worthwhile seeing.

results.title: Beautiful, but limited access and some damage
results.text:
I love this place and found myself there on many occasions. I didn’t give it an excellent review because you can’t really get close to the main temples unless you are Hindu and there can be some real pressure from people who try to trick you into guiding you, then guilting you. Be respectful and kind and it will take you far, but avoid the hard sell and tricksters. 
The Ghats are a must see and require walking around a bit, this is sacred space. Be sure to walk up the hill behind the Ghats opposite the river from the temple.

results.title: Humbling, cultural experience
results.text:
This is a beautiful part of Kathmandu that is full of Nepalese culture. There are cows, covered in flowers of worship, monkeys, sadhus (definitely worth getting a photo with these religious men - you can’t miss them - they’ll be very colourful but you’ll have to negotiate payment to pose with them). 
Some of the buildings surrounding the temple are suffering structural issues due to the earthquake a few years ago. It’s quite sad to see the devastating effect it has had.
The funeral pyres are also visible, lining the river. Throughout the morning, you will see bodies being prepared in the river, wrapped in orange garments and burnt upon the fires. Once completely burnt, the ashes are pushed into the river, which is difficult to see when, just further up stream, there are children playing and women washing their laundry.
If you’re in Kathmandu, this place is a must-visit.

results.title: Special place for end of a life journey
results.text: It is not usual to have a funeral under open special in asian country. You could learn the culture and traditions of Hindu"s funeral - that they burn dead bodies beside the river that they believe could wash their sin and bring them to afterlife. Stay quiet and respect people under the ceremony; and you could not enter the temple unless you are a Hindu.
